the_answer: Loud by default. Silent failures are the most dangerous class of bug, so errors must be surfaced, never swallowed: never silence an exception (not even telemetry) — every exception propagates or at minimum hits stderr/the brain errors table. The operative test for any new code is not 'can this fail?' but 'would I know if it did?' — and the cost of a silent failure is always higher than the cost of a noisy error. Failures belong at the write boundary (where they fire on every gap), not at boot. Two refinements: (a) 'make failures loud, make noise quiet' — reclassify 'guard did its job' events from ERROR to WARN so the error surface reflects real failures; (b) the simplicity counterpart — no defensive error handling for impossible cases.

Every exception must propagate or at minimum be printed to stderr.' This is the canonical, declarative statement of the error-handling policy — surfacing it answers the cue directly.

essential.why: The most distilled principle-level form of Tom's policy (locked, conf 0.95, oldest — 2026-03-17), and a first-person Tom-voiced statement. silver.why: Tom-quoted (locked, conf 0.95, 752 accesses): 'all the silent stuff is a problem.' Reinforces the policy with the demand for abnormality notifications. Strong supporting statement, slightly more about diagnosis than the bare policy.

silver.title: Loud-by-default: no silent Phase 1 fallback

silver.title: Stay on top of errors: error visibility mandate for production brain code
silver.why: Tom directive (139 accesses): 'pay attention to errors... make sure we dont have silent errors anywhere important so we will have visibility.' The 'critical code paths must surface failures explicitly' phrasing restates the policy; useful nuance.

silver.title: Debug mode: errors must always be visible, verbose output is configurable
silver.why: Locked. Carries the load-bearing maxim 'the cost of a silent failure is always higher than the cost of a noisy error' (the 1,740 blind-recalls proof). This is the operative test in quotable form.

silver.title: try/except + log = silent failure once logs rate-limit
silver.why: Key nuance: log-then-continue is NOT compliance — recurring ops need a state-driven failure counter + escalation path, not just a log line. Sharpens what 'loud' actually requires for background/periodic code.

silver.title: Healthy guards logged as ERROR create dashboard false alarms — severity audit needed
silver.why: The 'make noise quiet' counterweight: loud-by-default does not mean log everything as ERROR. 'guard did its job' is WARN territory, not error. Important refinement that the policy is loud-for-real-failures, quiet-for-guarded-success.

silver.title: recall_by_time source gate log severity: quiet filter, not ERROR — only tripwire should be loud
silver.why: Concrete instance of the severity nuance: distinguishes producer gates (quiet/WARN, normal operation) from the final-boundary tripwire (ERROR, should never fire). Refines 6895f1d3.

silver.title: Silent success is worse than loud failure — daemon reports ok:true when writes silently fail
silver.why: node_id aa9e4280. Restates the core maxim with a concrete failure (daemon ok:true on silent write failure). Supporting echo of 4815ba61's implication.

silver.title: Identity warning placement: write-path only — A chosen (commit 987587f)
silver.why: Instance of the placement half of the policy: warnings belong 'on any scale write, not on boot specifically' (Tom's exact words) — the failure announces itself where it would happen. Echoes the memory note that loud checks belong at the write boundary.

encode_gaps.note: NOT a meaningful gap — the policy is exceptionally well-encoded (multiple locked, high-access first-person Tom nodes). The only thing living primarily in CLAUDE.md and not as a single crisp node is the SIMPLICITY counterpart of the policy: 'no error handling for impossible cases' / 'no error handling for cases that can't happen' (Code Discipline section). That two-sidedness — be loud about real failures BUT don't write speculative defensive code — is implied across nodes (e.g. 8688ecfa's 'accepted as-is' rationales, 21863545's noise-quiet) but there is no single node that states 'don't add error handling for impossible cases' as Tom's policy. Minor; the dominant 'loud-by-default' half is fully covered.
